post.caption: Ireland's gold moon collars. A lunula is a flat crescent collar of gold, and the word means little moon. They are about 4,000 years old. More than 100 are known from western Europe, and more than 80 come from Ireland. Craftsmen hammered the gold into very thin sheet, and fine zigzag lines are densest at the tips. The Coggalbeg lunula was dug from a bog in 1945, and the National Museum of Ireland keeps it. Nobody knows exactly what they were for. A Cornish lunula and a Breton one are identical, and they may be the work of one craftsperson.
